The [[Florida Democratic Party|Democratic]] nominee was former Governor [[Charlie Crist]], who was Scott's direct predecessor. Crist was elected governor as a Republican in [[2006 Florida gubernatorial election|2006]] but did not run for re-election in 2010, instead opting to [[2010 United States Senate election in Florida|run for Senate]] as an [[Independent politician|independent]]. [[Libertarian Party of Florida|Libertarian]] nominee [[Adrian Wyllie]] and several candidates with no party affiliation also ran. Political pundits considered the race a toss-up. This was one of nine Republican-held governorships up for election in a state that [[Barack Obama]] won in the [[2012 United States presidential election|2012 presidential election]]. On October 22 it was reported that Scott's total spending had exceeded $83 million and he announced that, having previously said he would not do so, he would be investing his own money into the campaign, speculated to be as much as $22 million.{{cite web|url=http://miamiherald.typepad.com/nakedpolitics/2014/10/scott-says-he-will-write-his-campaign-a-personal-check-after-all-.html |title=Scott says he will write his campaign a personal check, after all, but won't say how much |publisher=Miami Herald |date=October 22, 2014 |access-date=October 23, 2014 |author=Marc Caputo}} Crist hoped to draw strong support from Florida's more than 1.6 million registered black voters, an effort that was challenging with regards to his previous political career as a Republican. A poll conducted in September 2014 by Quinnipiac University revealed his support among black voters was at 72 percent against Scott, which was below the 90 percent analysts believed he needed to win.{{cite news|last1=Stein|first1=Letitia|title=In Florida governor's race, Democrat woos crucial black vote|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-florida-election-idUSKBN0FZ17J20140730|access-date=September 15, 2014|work=Reuters|date=July 30, 2014}} Scott and Crist met in a debate on October 15, held by the Florida Press Association at [[Broward College]].{{cite web| url=http://beforeyouvote.org/| title=The race for the governor of florida| website=Before You Vote| access-date=October 5, 2014}} The debate required candidates to receive at least 15% support in major polls to be included. This was allegedly increased from 10% after Wyllie met the initial criteria,{{cite web| url=http://www.uncoveredpolitics.com/2014/09/18/despite-strong-polling-libertarian-barred-from-florida-gubernatorial-debate/| title=Despite Strong Polling, Libertarian Barred from Florida Gubernatorial Debate | date=September 18, 2014| website =Uncovered Politics| access-date =October 5, 2014}} but the ''Miami Herald'' reported that the threshold had been 15% since 2013.{{cite news | url=http://miamiherald.typepad.com/nakedpolitics/2014/10/libertarian-adrian-wyllie-sues-to-get-into-florida-press-association-debate.html | title=Libertarian Adrian Wyllie sues to get into Florida Press Association debate | work=Miami Herald | date=October 9, 2014 | author=Caputo. Marc}} The decision has been criticized as "suppressing choice"{{cite web| url=http://www.mynews13.com/content/news/cfnews13/news/article.html/content/news/articles/cfn/2014/10/3/opinion_wyllie_exclu.html| title=Opinion: Excluding Wyllie is suppressing voter choice| last=Ertel| first=Michelle| date=October 3, 2014| publisher=Central Florida News 13| access-date=October 5, 2014| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141005183839/http://mynews13.com/content/news/cfnews13/news/article.html/content/news/articles/cfn/2014/10/3/opinion_wyllie_exclu.html| archive-date=October 5, 2014| url-status=dead| df=mdy-all}} and the Wyllie campaign has filed a lawsuit to be included in the debate.{{cite web| url=http://www.mynews13.com/content/news/cfnews13/news/article.html/content/news/articles/cfn/2014/10/2/adrian_wyllie_shut_o.html| title=Adrian Wyllie shut out of debates, to sue organizers| last=Handiboe| first=John| date=October 2, 2014| publisher=Central Florida News 13| access-date =October 5, 2014}} U.S. District Judge [[James I.
